title: Power Dynamics and Hybrid Bus Modeling for DC Microgrids: A Structural Abstraction Approach
content: The massive integration of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) is radically transforming the structural and dynamic landscape of modern electric grids. Traditional power system modeling paradigms, heavily reliant on device-specific assumptions and synchronous generation dynamics, struggle to cope with the multi-scale, multi-domain complexities of renewable-dominated networks. To address these challenges, this paper provides a comprehensive review and a novel bottom-up synthesis of abstract modeling frameworks that distill core grid dynamics into device-independent, generalized formulations. By operating a structural reduction from traditional second-order circuit variables—such as node voltages (V), branch currents (I), and resistances (R)—this framework establishes an autonomous, first-order syntax governed exclusively by localized power variables (P) and efficiency metrics (η). Central to this abstraction is the formulation of the Hybrid Bus (Hbus), a virtual component with a rigorous mathematical foundation whose gnoseological and epistemological justification is addressed in a dedicated philosophical paper. The practical utility of this Power Dynamics approach is demonstrated through its application to power systems and distribution lines, offering a highly scalable blueprint for mapping complex networks evaluated through the lenses of mathematical generalization, topological scalability, and multi-temporal operation. Finally, a future perspective is outlined regarding the scalable extension of this framework into full matrix formulations for large-scale power network analysis.
